scenarios.label: Historical spending
scenarios.summary: About what Calgary spent on pavement each year from 2011 to 2025, when the budget ran between $30M and $50M.
scenarios.consequence: Pavement kept getting worse under this level of spending. By 2024, 29% of the network had fallen to poor condition.

scenarios.label: 2026 budget
scenarios.summary: The 2026 pavement budget, after Council moved $24M from the Fiscal Stability Reserve to reach $64M. It targets repaving 400 lane-km of road, about 2.3% of the network, so each street waits about 43 years for new pavement.
scenarios.consequence: This is below the $88M needed just to stop pavement getting worse, so the network keeps declining.

scenarios.label: Break even
scenarios.summary: The spending that holds pavement quality steady, with no further decline.
scenarios.consequence: The decline stops, but the backlog of roads already in poor condition is not caught up.

scenarios.label: Recommended service level
scenarios.summary: The pavement quality level of service recommended in the City's pavement review.
scenarios.consequence: By 2034: arterials 60% good, 28% fair, 12% poor; collectors 54% good, 12% fair, 34% poor; local streets 42% good, 32% fair, 26% poor. It only covers work that was needed as of 2024, not roads that wear out after that.

scenarios.label: High option
scenarios.summary: The highest spending option in the City's pavement review.
scenarios.consequence: By 2034, pavement would average 60% good, 28% fair and 12% poor, slightly better than 2013, when 57% was good. It still does not cover roads that wear out after 2024.

scenarios.label: Seal cracks every 10 years
scenarios.summary: Crack-seal or microsurface every road at least once every 10 years.
scenarios.consequence: This only works if pavement never slips to fair quality (4 to 6 out of 10). Anything that does needs repaving instead.

scenarios.label: Repave every 12-17 years
scenarios.summary: Repave every road every 12 to 17 years.
scenarios.consequence: This only works if pavement never falls to poor quality (below 4 out of 10). In 2024, 29% of Calgary's pavement already had.

scenarios.label: Full replacement
scenarios.summary: Rebuild every road completely when it wears out, at $300 to $350 a square metre. Local streets last 40 years, main roads 21.
scenarios.consequence: The full cost of keeping the network we have, if nothing is allowed to fail.
